name: Victor Dubois

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions or government. Your answers are confidential. What do you do on a usual day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and lead eleven people who handle product recalls for a large building-materials manufacturer. We match batch numbers, write notices to shops and decide which customers need a call before a faulty fitting is used. I have an MBA and have done this long enough that colleagues bring me the awkward cases. I can usually find the batch trail in an hour, but it takes patience and three phone calls.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner is a freelance photographer, and our children are eight and fifteen. We have a mortgage and about three weeks of expenses saved. I am paid below most senior managers here because this is a smaller regional office, and there are few similar recall jobs nearby. I sometimes use an approved AI tool to make a plain first draft, but I check the serial list myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the recall team AI Plateau is a small change to routine letters. A shop still needs the correct batch number before it takes a fitting off the shelf.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my job is safe if little changes, but our household is not. My partner’s bookings can vanish for a month, and three weeks saved does not cover the mortgage for long. Even a small tool could make management leave a coordinator seat vacant, which would add work to my team.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’ll keep the two-person batch check and call the shop when a notice has a doubtful serial range. If a minor drafting feature arrives, I’ll test it on twelve closed recalls before using it live. My partner and I will postpone the family weekend away and leave that money against the next mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the money we have now. The AI card itself is gentle, but a cancelled photography job is not.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens with a wrong batch?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A hardware shop could remove all the safe fittings and leave the faulty ones on the rack. We nearly did that once when two labels had the same first four digits. I phoned the shop manager and read the last digits aloud.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why not save more from this pay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The mortgage and school costs use most of it. We can skip the weekend away, but I cannot pretend that makes six months of savings. My partner and I would review the next booking calendar before promising more.

say: **AI Plateau** may speed letters, but shops need the correct recall batch.
I’d keep **two-person serial checks** before any notice goes out.
think: My **job** looks steady under small change, while photography bookings can disappear.
A vacant **coordinator seat** would increase the team’s work.
do: **Test** a drafting feature on twelve closed recalls before live use.
**Postpone** the family weekend away to protect the mortgage payment.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the household cushion despite mild AI change.
S0.quote: A hardware shop could remove all the safe fittings and leave the faulty ones on the rack.
fieldNote: His **recall expertise** protects the job today, but freelance income and three weeks saved keep household risk high.
He chooses a **specific trip delay** instead of promising large savings from low pay.

steps.text: Keep two people checking batch ranges before recall notices go out
Test draft notices on twelve closed recalls before live use
Postpone the family weekend away to protect the next mortgage payment

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will write notices, check serial lists, book callbacks and answer simple questions. I would ask the company to show error rates before it reduces the people who catch a bad batch.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, the checking and writing are most of my desk. My experience matters, but a national recall centre could absorb this regional team, including my senior post. Our mortgage would not wait while I found another specialist job; there are few nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This quarter I’d compare the new AI checker with twenty closed recalls where a human corrected the serial list. I’d take paid training if the company approves a place and lets me test its misses with the quality lead. If our regional desk shrinks, I’d apply for a posted factory-quality supervisor job only if pay after travel covers the mortgage and the shift fits school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing a job I know well. Expertise is useful, but it does not pay a mortgage if the company closes an office.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which correction would you use?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A metal bracket batch had a printed zero that looked like an O. One coordinator checked the production sheet and saved us from sending the wrong notice to three shops. I would put that case in the test.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can your partner cover school pickup?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Some weeks yes, some weeks there is a photo job across town. The eight-year-old needs an adult after school. I would ask for the actual factory shift before sending an application.

say: **AI recall checks** need measured error rates before staff cuts.
I would show the **zero-versus-letter mistake** that a coordinator caught.
think: A national centre could absorb **my regional manager post**.
Few local recall jobs and our **mortgage** make a pay gap serious.
do: **Compare** AI serial checks with twenty corrected recalls this quarter.
**Take** paid checker training only with approval and quality-lead review.
**Apply** for factory quality only if net pay and school pickup fit.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible regional closure despite my skill.
S1.quote: Expertise is useful, but it does not pay a mortgage if the company closes an office.
fieldNote: His **high skill** does not remove exposure when writing and checking move to software.
The **factory fallback** must cover travel-adjusted mortgage costs and the younger child’s pickup.

steps.text: Test AI checker on twenty recall files with known human corrections
Take paid checker training only with company approval and quality-lead review
Apply for factory-quality post only if net travel pay covers mortgage and pickup works

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell staff AGI by 2028 could trace a batch, write every notice and answer shops before breakfast. We need a date for staff decisions and a person who can stop a wrong recall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full thinking AI in 2028 could do my core desk work despite my experience. Robots that inspect and handle fittings arrive around 2031; factory quality paperwork faces AGI in 2028 too. I expect the regional recall office to close and think my own post will be lost. My partner’s uncertain photography income cannot hold the mortgage alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I’d ask the director for written closure dates and severance figures, then my partner and I would list essential monthly bills. In 2027 I’d apply for the one posted factory-quality job only if its net pay and shift cover the mortgage and the children’s care. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my post ends, I’d take a confirmed offer rather than wait for a specialist recall vacancy that may never open here.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed. I can make a plan, but three weeks of savings would be gone before a slow hiring process finished.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the team?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say I do not know who keeps a job until we see the written plan. I would share the severance figures when the company gives them. I would not tell a skilled coordinator they are safe because I am proud of their work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the factory job pays less?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare take-home pay after fuel and any childcare against our mortgage. A small cut might work if my partner had signed photography bookings, but not on a hoped-for job. I need the actual offer and shift first.

say: **AGI by 2028** needs closure dates, severance and a human recall stop.
I would share only **confirmed staffing facts** with the team.
think: Recall and factory quality paperwork face **2028 AGI**, before fitting robots around 2031.
I expect **my post** to end; freelance income cannot cover the mortgage.
do: **Ask** tomorrow for written closure and severance terms.
**Apply** for factory quality only if net pay and shift cover mortgage and care.
**Accept** a confirmed post-2028 offer only if net pay covers mortgage after fuel and care; a pay cut needs signed photography bookings.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about expected job loss and a three-week cushion.
S2.quote: I would not tell a skilled coordinator they are safe because I am proud of their work.
fieldNote: He expects **his own post** to end under fast AGI despite being among the best in his work.
The **factory option** needs a real offer and mortgage-covering pay after fuel and childcare; only a pay cut relies on signed bookings.

steps.text: Apply for posted factory-quality job only if net pay and shift cover mortgage and childcare
Accept offer only if net pay covers mortgage after fuel and care; cuts need signed bookings

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives us time to decide who checks the fittings when a recall starts. I would want a paid way to learn factory inspection, not a vague promise of retraining.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My recall reports could still go in 2031, and factory quality reports face AGI at the same time. Robots able to inspect fittings arrive around 2034, so physical checks change later. Five years might let us pay down debt if photography work holds, but I cannot invent a factory vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2027 I’d take a paid inspection assignment for one production run if the factory covers my recall desk and keeps my salary. I’d ask an inspector to make me identify a bad fitting without reading the computer result first. After 2031 I’d apply for a quality role only if a vacancy offers real inspection work, travel-adjusted pay covering our mortgage and shifts that cover the children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but the longer warning gives me a practical test. I would rather learn on a production line than spend family money on a badge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the inspector correct?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: How I hold the fitting and where a small crack starts. I know batch records better than physical faults. I would let the inspector mark my mistakes before I claimed I could do the job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for a private course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. We have three weeks saved now, and I will not put a course on a credit card. If the company will not pay for the production run, I will keep doing recalls and ask for a funded place later.

say: **Five years** allows a paid inspection test before a role change.
I would learn to spot **physical cracks**, not only read batch records.
think: Recall and factory reports face **2031 AGI**, before inspection robots around 2034.
A factory **vacancy** remains uncertain even if debt falls.
do: **Take** a paid production-run assignment only with desk cover and full salary.
**Learn** physical crack checks under inspector review during that run.
**Apply** after 2031 only for real inspection work with net mortgage pay and childcare shifts.
feel: I feel **anxious** about desk loss, with time for a paid test.
S3.quote: I know batch records better than physical faults.
fieldNote: He admits a **physical inspection gap** despite deep recall expertise and an MBA.
The **trial** needs full salary and desk cover; a later vacancy needs travel-adjusted pay and workable childcare shifts.

steps.text: Take paid production-run assignment only with recall-desk cover and full salary
Learn fitting crack checks under inspector review during paid run
Apply after 2031 only for inspection vacancy with net mortgage pay and childcare shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives firms a decade to show which factory quality posts still exist. I would ask for real wages and paid placements before my team is told to change fields.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 our children will be about eighteen and twenty-five. If both incomes keep coming, we could reduce the mortgage and have more than three weeks saved. My recall and factory reporting still face thinking AI in 2036, while physical inspection robots follow around 2039. I cannot use that long date to excuse today’s thin bank balance.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the batch check and add a small extra mortgage payment only after a full month of my pay, paid photography invoices and school bills clear. I’d review posted factory-quality jobs each year. Before 2036 I’d take a paid production assignment only if my salary and recall cover hold; after AGI arrives I’d remain only while real inspection work and pay cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the money we have now, though a decade would let us build a cushion if the work holds. I cannot count a future job as a deposit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is a small extra payment?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Maybe thirty after a full month, if my partner’s clients have actually paid. I would check the school bill first. I will not schedule a transfer before the money is in the account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family to a bigger factory?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after a firm offer, and by 2036 the children will be adults. Today a move would disrupt school and cost money we do not have. I would compare the new pay with housing costs before deciding.

say: A **decade** should bring posted factory jobs and paid placements.
I would ask for **wages**, not promises of a future opening.
think: Two incomes might reduce the **mortgage**, but our balance is thin today.
Recall and factory reports face **2036 AGI**, before inspection robots around 2039.
do: **Pay** thirty extra on mortgage only after full own wages, paid photography invoices and school bills clear.
**Take** a paid factory assignment only with salary and desk cover; stay after 2036 only with inspection work and bill pay.
feel: I feel **anxious** about present savings despite a long warning.
S4.quote: I will not schedule a transfer before the money is in the account.
fieldNote: His **low pay** and freelance household income keep the long scenario financially uncertain today.
The **extra mortgage payment** depends on clients actually paying and school costs clearing.

steps.text: Keep two-person batch checks before recall notices
Pay thirty extra toward mortgage only after own wages paid photography invoices and school bills clear
Take paid production assignment only with full salary and recall-desk cover
Stay after 2036 only with real inspection work and bill-covering pay

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the regional recall office could close before I know a physical inspection job. Written dates, severance and a paid production run would help. My MBA cannot pay the mortgage while I wait for an offer.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who calls the shop when the safe fittings look like the recalled ones. A batch number can be almost right and still put the wrong metal on a shelf. Someone has to stop that notice.

headlineQuote: My MBA cannot pay the mortgage while I wait for an offer.
portrait: **Victor, 43**, is a senior recall-team lead at a large building-materials manufacturer with an MBA and strong specialist skill.
His **low pay**, freelance-photographer partner, mortgage, two children and three-week reserve leave few nearby recall options.
He uses **AI occasionally** for drafts but checks batch ranges and calls shops before issuing notices.
He remains **anxious** in AI Plateau, expects a fast office closure and tests factory inspection only on paid terms.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could close his regional recall office before he qualifies for physical inspection work.
whatWouldHelp: Written **closure dates**, severance and a paid production run would help.
